answer: Like a lagoon that only admits boats through one narrow channel, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade. A sybil operator who spawns a gale of fake agents must fund every one, so the cost scales with the attack. An onyx-hard rule then slashes the stake of any identity caught misbehaving, turning fake identities from free camouflage into a money-losing liability.
